record.paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
record.original_question: For the boundary-value problem for an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium governed by equations (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), and the objective-derivative constitutive law (2.18), does the initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution in dimensions n ≥ 2 without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?

evidence.quote: К первой группе относятся проблема сильной глобальной разрешимости начально-краевой задачи, проблема регулярности слабых решений, проблема единственности слабых решений, оценка хаусдорфовой размерности траекторных и глобальных аттракторов3 (все эти задачи требуют решения без ограничений на коэффициенты, внешнюю силу и начальные данные).
Важно, что для Навье-Стокса эти задачи актуальны при n ≥ 3, а для (0.2),(0.4),(0.5),(2.18) — при n ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $T>0$. Consider the initial-boundary value problem for an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys type, in which the velocity field $v:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^n$, the pressure $p:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}$, and the extra (deviatoric) stress tensor $\sigma:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_{\mathrm{sym}}$ satisfy:

(i) The momentum balance and incompressibility:
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)v - \nu\,\Delta v + \nabla p = \operatorname{Div}\sigma + f, \qquad \operatorname{div} v = 0,\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),$$
where $\nu>0$ is a Newtonian viscosity and $f$ is a given external body force.

(ii) The no-slip boundary condition and initial data:
$$v\big|_{\partial\Omega} = 0,\qquad v\big|_{t=0} = v_0\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad \sigma\big|_{t=0}=\sigma_0\quad\text{in }\Omega,$$
with $\operatorname{div} v_0 = 0$.

(iii) A Jeffreys-type constitutive law for $\sigma$ involving an objective (frame-indifferent) time derivative $\mathcal{D}_a$ of the form
$$\mathcal{D}_a \sigma := \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)\sigma + \sigma\,W(v) - W(v)\,\sigma - a\bigl(\sigma\,E(v)+E(v)\,\sigma\bigr),$$
where $E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^\top)$, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v-\nabla v^\top)$, and $a\in[-1,1]$ is a fixed parameter, and the relation
$$\sigma + \lambda\,\mathcal{D}_a\sigma = 2\eta\,E(v),$$
with positive relaxation time $\lambda$ and elastic viscosity $\eta>0$.

A strong solution on $[0,T]$ is a triple $(v,p,\sigma)$ such that $v\in L^\infty(0,T;H^1_0(\Omega)^n)\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\Omega)^n)$ with $\partial_t v\in L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$, $\sigma\in L^\infty(0,T;H^1(\Omega)^{n\times n})$ with $\partial_t\sigma\in L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$, the equations hold a.e., and the initial conditions are attained.

Question: For every $n\ge 2$, every bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, every $T>0$, and arbitrary positive coefficients $\nu,\lambda,\eta$, parameter $a\in[-1,1]$, external force $f$ in a natural class (e.g. $L^2(0,T;L^2(\Omega)^n)$), and arbitrary admissible initial data $(v_0,\sigma_0)$, does the above initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution on $[0,T]$, with no smallness or other restriction on the data, coefficients, or force?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (including a 2025 study of flow-through problems for Jeffreys fluids with objective derivatives and surveys on viscoelastic models) explicitly notes that for differential viscoelastic models with an objective time derivative in the constitutive law, no global strong solvability results without restrictions on data are known. Even global weak existence for related incompressible viscoelastic systems is described as a longstanding open problem. No source confirms a resolution of the unrestricted global strong solvability problem in dimensions $n\ge 2$.

status_evidence.title: Flow-through problem for a Jeffreys type viscoelastic fluid
status_evidence.snippet: For differential models of viscoelastic fluids with objective derivatives in a constitutive law, there are no such results in the existing scientific literature.
status_evidence.claim: No global solvability results without data restrictions are known for Jeffreys-type models with objective derivatives.

status_evidence.title: Global existence in critical spaces for incompressible viscoelastic fluids
status_evidence.snippet: The global existence of solutions to the incompressible viscoelastic flows has been a longstanding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Global existence for incompressible viscoelastic flows remains a longstanding open problem in general.

status_evidence.title: Dissipative solvability of Jeffreys-Oldroyd-α model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a regularized (alpha) Jeffreys-Oldroyd model, indicating the original system's strong solvability is not established without modification.
status_evidence.claim: Available results require regularization or restrictions, supporting that the unrestricted problem is open.
